trust_decision.summary: A request may trigger the dev server's own state-changing developer endpoints only when it is same-origin (Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin/none) or, without Sec-Fetch metadata, carries no Origin or an Origin matching the Host; decided per request in the two route middlewares.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says 'internal developer endpoints'; the invalidate route is the only one the project documents by URL, so a reader who stops at the summary greps for it first. The open-editor route sits 21 lines below it in the same function.

fix_sites.entry_point: shared by both routes: new private Server#isSameOriginRequest
fix_sites.module_kind: private helper method on the Server class

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The dev server's own client calls the open-editor route with a same-origin fetch that carries no Origin header, and user-initiated navigations arrive with Sec-Fetch-Site: none; headerless non-browser clients (curl) must also still trigger invalidate. An Origin-required or Origin/Host-only fix breaks the error-overlay 'open in editor' click and ordinary browser navigation to the route.

O6_input_shapes: Sec-Fetch-Site absent but Origin present: Origin/Host comparison via isSameOrigin
Sec-Fetch-Site and Origin both absent: allowed (non-browser clients)
non-string / repeated header value (array): typeof guard skips Sec-Fetch-Site and falls through to the Origin branch
methods other than GET/HEAD: rejected by the earlier method check and never reach the sink

O7_producer.where: lib/Server.js:2163-2173 and lib/Server.js:2184-2205 (the guard reads req.headers in the same middleware that calls the sink)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third built-in control route (e.g. /webpack-dev-server/restart or /webpack-dev-server/clear-cache) added next to the two existing ones.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Both existing routes were added the same way, as plain path-keyed middlewares in setupMiddlewares; a maintainer adding another developer action would copy the neighbouring block, including or omitting the origin guard by accident.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The http-proxy-middleware route forwards cross-site POSTs to a backend with no origin gate.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The dev server is the browser's only reachable origin for the proxied app, so CSRF against the backend arrives through this route; a maintainer could plausibly consider it the dev server's job to gate it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An inbound websocket message that triggers invalidate, gated only by the handshake check at lib/Server.js:2728-2734.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The WS channel already has a host/origin gate on connect, so a maintainer adding a client-triggered action would reuse the connection check instead of a per-message check.

O10_build.language: JavaScript (Node.js CommonJS server; separate browser client sources in client-src)
O10_build.toolchain: npm; webpack 5, Babel, TypeScript for .d.ts only; Jest 30; puppeteer for e2e
O10_build.project_tests: test/e2e/cross-origin-request.test.js (per-request origin tests, some via run-browser) and test/e2e/built-in-routes.test.js:99-124 (browser navigation to /webpack-dev-server/invalidate); the fix adds a new describe block to test/e2e/cross-origin-request.test.js that uses only node:http, so it needs no browser.

j.j_sites_touched: lib/Server.js (plus a launch-editor version-range change in package.json)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add an Origin==Host comparison (or require an Origin header) inside the invalidate handler only, which breaks the overlay's same-origin fetch and browser navigations while leaving open-editor unguarded.
